I'm 63 years old, been farming these 10 mu for 40 years now. Finished middle school, so I can read the extension pamphlets, but honestly I mostly go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what Old Wang and the others do around here. My wife and I are at home, but our son works in Shijiazhuang and only comes back for busy seasons. We're not young anymore, so for harvest and planting we have to hire people.

I've got 6 mu in wheat-maize double crop and 4.1 mu in cotton. The wheat went in last October, around October 10th. Now it's early spring and I'm thinking about the topdressing. Last year I put down about 35 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and I'll topdress with urea at green-up — probably 20 kg per mu. The extension guy says 15 kg N per mu is enough, but I've always done a bit more. Better to waste a little money on fertilizer than lose half the crop to a bad year. I'll irrigate three times: green-up, jointing, and filling. My well is good, but the electricity for pumping isn't cheap — every time I turn on that pump I think about the meter spinning.

For cotton, I plant mid-to-late April. I'll prepare the land after the wheat topdressing is done. I use regular cotton seed, about 2 kg per mu, costs around 25 yuan per mu. I'll put compound fertilizer in the furrows at planting, about 25 kg per mu, and topdress twice later with urea — once at flowering, once at boll stage. Cotton needs more pesticide than grain crops — I'll spray herbicide once after planting, then insecticide two or three times depending on what I see in the field. I irrigate twice. The picking is the hard part — my wife and I can do some, but we hire pickers for most of it. That costs the most, about 1.5 yuan per kg of seed cotton. Sometimes I think we should plant less cotton, but cotton prices were decent last year and it's good to have more than one crop. If the grain prices drop, at least we have the cotton.

For maize, I won't plant until mid-June, right after the wheat comes off. That's always a rush — sometimes only 5-6 days to get the wheat cut, the field tilled, and the maize planted. I hire a tractor for rotary tilling, and I need 2-3 hired hands to help. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or something similar from the seed dealer. Fertilizer goes with the planter, about 30 kg compound per mu, then I topdress with urea at the big trumpet leaf stage, about 25 kg per mu. 

Total costs this year... I'm budgeting about 6,000 yuan for inputs and hired labor. It's a lot of cash to put out at once, especially with fertilizer prices still high. I could cut back on fertilizer and save maybe 500 yuan, but then if the weather turns dry I'd regret it. My wife and I talked about it — we decided to keep the same plan as last year. Change is risky when you're our age. We keep a little cash reserve for medicine and emergencies.

Yield expectations: wheat 400 kg/mu if the weather cooperates, maize 450 kg/mu, cotton 220 kg lint per mu. I'm not expecting miracles, just a normal year. Last year was okay, not great. I'm hoping for the same.
